column1: General linear group over a commutative ring
column5: For a commutative ring W and k>=0, GL_k(W) is the group of k x k matrices over W with an inverse matrix over W, equivalently with determinant a unit of W.
column6: Commutative ring; Matrix; Determinant; Unit of a ring

column5: For a finite family of square matrices A_s over a commutative ring, indexed by s in S, the Kronecker product is the matrix indexed by families (beta_s), (alpha_s) with entry prod_s (A_s)_{beta_s, alpha_s}; it is the matrix of the tensor product of the linear maps.

For a k x k matrix A over a commutative ring R and n>=0, Sym^n(A) is the matrix indexed by exponents of degree n in k variables whose (beta, alpha) entry is the coefficient of x^beta in the image of x^alpha under the substitution x_c -> sum_b A_{b,c} x_b; it is multiplicative in A.
A polynomial in several variables over a commutative ring all of whose monomials with nonzero coefficient have the same total degree d.
A commutative ring O such that for all x, y in O, x divides y or y divides x; here always also an integral domain. A valuation ring is local.
For an exponent gamma = (gamma_i) with finite support and total degree d, the integer d! / prod_i gamma_i!; it is a product of binomial coefficients.
In a commutative ring, (sum_i x_i)^d = sum over exponents gamma of degree d of multinomial(gamma) prod_i x_i^{gamma_i}.
The p-adic valuation of binomial(n+m, n) is the number of carries when adding n and m in base p; in particular it is at most log_p(n+m) (floor). Only the bound is used.
column6: Binomial coefficient; p-adic valuation of an integer

column5: If M is a finitely generated module over a local ring W with maximal ideal m and M = mM, then M = 0. Form used: a submodule V of a finite module M is everything if every W-linear map from M/V to the residue field is zero.
column6: Local ring; Finitely generated module; Maximal ideal; Residue field

column1: Vanishing of homogeneous polynomials on a finite field
column5: A homogeneous polynomial of degree d in finitely many variables over a field with at least d elements that vanishes at every point is the zero polynomial.

For a commutative ring O and k, d >= 0, the Schur algebra S(k,d) is the algebra of endomorphisms of (O^k)^{tensor d} commuting with the symmetric group; equivalently the dual of the polynomials of degree d in the matrix entries. Here: for a labelling tau, the image of the map sending a linear form l on monomials of degree d to the d-th tensor power of the generic block matrix with l applied entrywise.
column6: Tensor power of a module; Polynomial ring; Levi subgroup

column5: The d-fold tensor product of a module with itself over the base ring; for a free module with basis e_0..e_{k-1} it is free with basis the tensors e_j, j in {0..k-1}^d.
column6: Tensor product of modules; Free module

column5: For matrices A (m x n) and B (n x m) over a commutative ring, det(1_m - AB) = det(1_n - BA) (Sylvester's determinant identity).
det M = sum over permutations sigma of sgn(sigma) prod_b M_{sigma(b), b}.
The homomorphism from the symmetric group of a finite set to {1,-1} sending every transposition to -1.

column1: Change of variables for Lebesgue measure under a linear map
column5: For an invertible linear endomorphism L of R^n and a set A, vol(L^{-1}(A)) = |det L|^{-1} vol(A) for Lebesgue measure.
For indices a != a' and an element x of a commutative ring, the matrix 1 + x E_{a,a'}, which has determinant 1.

Form used (New.levi): for a labelling tau of {0..k-1} by natural numbers and a commutative ring W, the subgroup of GL_k(W) of matrices whose (i,j) entry is zero whenever tau(i) != tau(j) (block diagonal matrices for the fibres of tau).
column6: General linear group over a commutative ring

column5: Form used (New.parahoric): for a local ring W and a labelling tau, the subgroup of GL_k(W) of matrices whose (i,j) entry lies in the maximal ideal whenever tau(i) < tau(j).
column6: General linear group over a commutative ring; Local ring; Maximal ideal

column5: A commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal.
The quotient of a local ring by its maximal ideal.
The ring of polynomials in a set of variables over a commutative ring.
A map of rings preserving sums, products and 1.
An additive subgroup of a commutative ring closed under multiplication by ring elements.
A proper ideal not contained in a larger proper ideal.
A nonzero commutative ring without zero divisors.
A subset of a module closed under addition and scalar multiplication.
A module with a basis. Fact used: a finitely generated torsion-free module over a valuation domain is free.
The translation-invariant measure on R^n giving the unit cube volume 1 (product measure on functions Fin k x T -> R).
The trace of an endomorphism of a finite free module: the sum of the diagonal entries of its matrix in any basis; tr(AB) = tr(BA).
The determinant of a square matrix over a commutative ring.
